newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea plans one trillion won REPO deal.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea plans one trillion won REPO deal.

text.p: The Bank of Korea (BOK) plans to release one trillion won through repurchase agreements, BOK officials said on Tuesday.
They said the move would prevent tight liquidity in the short-term market following moves by creditor banks to bail out Kia Group.
An official at the central bank, who declined to be identified, said Kia had sought a bail-out.

"We plan to provide one trillion won to the banking system in view of possible tight liquidity following the application by Kia Group for protection against debt repayment defaults," a central bank official said.
He noted that some commercial banks were facing difficulties meeting reserve requirements.
A tender for one-day repurchase agreements was due at 3.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), he added.
At Kia Group's request, its creditor banks on Tuesday selected 18 of its 38 affiliates for a bail-out, the Korea First Bank said as the main creditor.
